instruction: List all model names from "~/Documents/awesome-desktop/expe-results.xlsx" as a table in the "Main Results" section of the report.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent scrolled through Writer doc, opened Calc, navigated to expe-results.xlsx, selected GPT-4 row, switched to Writer at 'Main Results' section, inserted a partial table with only 7 of 12 columns and no headers.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open files cross-app (Writer/Calc), read xlsx data, navigate Writer document sections, insert tables into specific sections
metadata.failure_analysis: Table was incomplete - only first 7 columns pasted (model through gimp), missing chrome/thunderbird/vscode/multi/avg columns and header row.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to only require listing model names from xlsx in the Main Results section. Model demonstrated ability to read xlsx and insert content, this focuses on that core capability.
metadata.explanation: Task requires listing model names from xlsx in Main Results section. Getter reads docx tables and section text. Metric checks for both model names: Gpt-4 (0.5) and rl+il (0.5).

scoring_breakdown.gpt4_name: 0.5 - Contains 'Gpt-4' in table or Main Results text
scoring_breakdown.rlil_name: 0.5 - Contains 'rl+il' in table or Main Results text

llm_judge_reasons: Metric parameter handling is correct: expected.get('model_names') directly accesses the rules dict as expected when type='rule'.
Getter correctly reads docx file, extracts all tables and 'Main Results' section text. Postconfig properly saves the file before extraction.
Case-insensitive matching for model names is appropriate and robust.
Tables are extracted globally from the entire document, not scoped to the 'Main Results' section. A table with model names in a different section would incorrectly count as a pass.
Instruction requires content 'as a table' but the metric also accepts plain paragraph text in the Main Results section. An agent that types model names as plain text (no table) would still pass.
Partial credit scoring (0.5 per model name) is reasonable for a 2-name check.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Scope table extraction to only tables that appear within the 'Main Results' section, not all tables in the document. This could be done by tracking paragraph/table ordering relative to section headings.
Add a check that at least one table exists in or near the 'Main Results' section to enforce the 'as a table' requirement from the instruction, rather than accepting plain text as sufficient.
